skills.name: Tell a personal ability, talent or interest and how to use it well

skills.name: Choose personal values that make a steady personality
skills.mastery: The child says a personal value is a belief about what is right that guides how a person acts (honesty, respect, responsibility, perseverance, kindness, integrity), tells values from possessions, and says a steady person keeps their values when friends pressure them to do wrong. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

skills.name: Tell the traditional stories of human origin that African communities hold
skills.mastery: The child tells that African communities hold their own stories of how people began, for example the Agikuyu story of Gikuyu and Mumbi under the Mukuru wa Gathanga tree given by Ngai, and the Maasai story that Enkai sent down cattle; that they were told aloud by elders; and that each community values its own. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
